scope: Owner-requested review of three local sandbox repositories for ScopeHub reuse
method: Static inspection of source, manifests, licenses, test examples and upstream project pages

recommendation.whole_application_adoption: Not established by this review. Reconsider if a product trial, license fit and representative workflow demonstrate lower lifetime cost than selective reuse.
recommendation.architecture: Existing language choices are provisional. These sources provide useful patterns and candidates, but static inspection alone does not justify replacing the runtime or authorization contract.

repositories.role: Primary reference for the first chart-and-AI workflow

license.name: OpenChart License: modified Apache-2.0 with additional conditions
observations: The license conditions multi-tenant operation on written authorization and includes frontend logo and copyright restrictions.
The tenant definition refers to a workspace. Do not assume that this only concerns a hosted SaaS deployment.
Do not classify this source as ordinary Apache-2.0 or copy it under ScopeHub's MIT notice alone. Source adoption needs a concrete use-specific license assessment.

candidates.capability: Research a selected chart interval using bounded factual context and source-linked annotations
candidates.use: Design reference for M4 context and chart operations

candidates.capability: One resource catalog shared by UI/API operations and AI tools, with revision-aware mutations
candidates.use: Reference for M2/M4 operation registry and concurrent edits

candidates.capability: Approval lifecycle, deny precedence, cancellation and persisting a grant before releasing a waiting tool
candidates.use: Reference for M2/M4 state transitions; retain ScopeHub's operation-specific permission contract

candidates.capability: Bounded indicator execution returning actual values and diagnostics with scoped resource cleanup
candidates.use: Reference for M3 preview and M4 AI inspection, without adopting Tea by default

integration_costs: The full product uses an Electron host, a Node/Effect server, tRPC resources, its own chart engine and the Tea language. Reusing the application would be a deliberate architecture choice.
chart-core imports workspace feed/market packages and Effect. It is not an isolated drop-in replacement for the planned chart adapter.
Chart Explain filters non-positive OHLC values. Its assumptions must not become universal constraints for future instruments.
Saved wildcard grants and generic resource writes must not silently replace ScopeHub's version-bound approvals and operation policies.
repositories.data_observation: Registered provider families are Binance, yfinance, OpenChart and local workspace datasets. This review did not validate Chinese futures or A-share service coverage.

repositories.role: Selective financial computation and data-quality candidate

license.name: Apache-2.0 for the main project and Desktop code
observations: Selected source may be a practical reuse candidate with applicable license, attribution and modification notices preserved; inspect the selected files and their dependency licenses before incorporation.

Desktop skill attribution reports converted Anthropic material as MIT, while the current upstream financial-services LICENSE is Apache-2.0. The conversion metadata contains no upstream commit. Resolve the historical source and license for any selected skill instead of relying on the parent project's license.

repositories.version_observation: The repository contains Desktop V2 (PydanticAI/FastAPI/React/Tauri), Equity V1 and AutoGen V0. Its README says pip install finrobot installs V0; package-name similarity is not evidence of installing Desktop V2.

candidates.capability: Structured data provenance and degradation, separate data time from fetch time, preserve stale-cache and stale-history distinctions
candidates.use: Reference for M1 data semantics and later real-provider adapters

candidates.capability: Cross-provider numerical checks with explicit field comparability and unavailable-source handling
candidates.use: Selective adapter/validation candidate when financial research data is introduced

candidates.capability: Deterministic valuation operators separated from AI-selected assumptions and narrative
candidates.use: Candidate for an optional Python research module when a concrete valuation workflow needs it

integration_costs: The full Desktop runtime includes FastAPI, its own SQLite ownership and agent/pipeline orchestration. Importing the whole package would bring responsibilities that do not match the current worker contract.
DCF depends on FinRobot financial models and valuation thresholds. Pure arithmetic does not make every operator an independently packaged library.
NormalizedPrice is built around dated bars and a trailing-year equity research view. Do not adopt it as the universal intraday or futures model.
The asymmetric beta adjustment and validation tolerances encode financial assumptions. Expose and validate such assumptions instead of inheriting them as market facts.

The numeric-grounding audit detects surviving digits after simple exclusions; it does not verify that a cited number matches evidence. Deterministic computation and warnings do not establish investment correctness.
The README describes Desktop as production, while its package classifier is Alpha. Runtime reliability remains unverified in this assessment.
repositories.data_observation: The inspected Desktop chain uses FMP, Finnhub, yfinance, SEC EDGAR, Adanos and a news aggregator as configured. This is not verified Chinese futures or A-share market access.

license.name: GNU AGPL version 3
observations: This is not an MIT source dependency. Any proposed source incorporation must account for the applicable AGPL obligations; this review adopts no source.

candidates.capability: Instrument search, watchlist presentation and visible data age
candidates.use: Interaction reference when these UI needs arise

integration_costs: Its charts load remote TradingView widget scripts. This hook does not provide the application-owned series and indicator-layer interface needed for ScopeHub's initial workflow.
Next.js, MongoDB, authentication and email jobs serve a web dashboard product. The inspected AI integration generates welcome/news email text, rather than exposing chart operations.
The Live label is selected by a global polling mode. Poll frequency alone does not verify the timeliness of a particular provider response.
Watchlist assembly substitutes zero for missing quotes and unknown P/E. Missing data must remain distinguishable from a real zero in ScopeHub.
repositories.data_observation: The market catalog is constrained by Finnhub and TradingView embed support. Its international-market UI does not establish the required Chinese futures or A-share coverage.

follow_up_candidates.action: Exercise actual data timestamps, cache age, missing values and mixed quote/history freshness in the simulated provider workflow; derive chart status from the data contract.
Use the permission and revision lifecycle examples when implementing shared human/AI operations; test cancellation while approval is pending and revisions changing before execution.

Complete the selected workflow: chart context, AI-generated indicator draft, bounded preview, inspectable output, authorized acceptance and chart annotation. Use OpenChart's workflow as a comparison target.

For a requested valuation or filing workflow, first evaluate a small FinRobot operator or provider adapter against ScopeHub's inputs and expected outputs; compare direct package use with an attributed source extraction.

Evaluate provider entitlements, coverage, delay, calendars, sessions and contract/adjustment semantics for Chinese futures, A-shares and US equities. Source-code licensing does not grant market-data rights.
